summary: Very thin day: Reddit, X and Bluesky were all blocked, so only Hacker News comments could be verified, and only two ideas reached the 2-source bar. Themes: people want a user-controlled filter for AI slop, Shorts and unwanted topics across sites, and AI-plan subscribers want clear, always-visible usage-limit information.

ideas.title: Mute Anything: one topic and AI-slop filter for HN, YouTube and the web
ideas.oneLiner: A browser extension that lets you mute topics (like AI), Shorts and flagged slop on Hacker News, YouTube and other feeds, with shared crowdsourced block lists.
ideas.problem: Users keep asking for a SponsorBlock-style way to filter out AI slop, AI-topic threads and Shorts. Existing extensions are single-site (HN source filter, YouTube AI-label hiders) and mostly rely on platform self-labels, so unlabeled content slips through.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy HN, YouTube and Reddit users, especially developers and creators fatigued by AI content.
ideas.monetization: Free core with local keyword and channel muting; Pro at about $3/month or $25/year for synced rules, shared community block lists and custom site rules.
mvp: Keyword and topic mute rules applied to HN, YouTube and Reddit feeds
Hide YouTube Shorts and videos from user-flagged channels
One-click 'mark as slop' button that adds an item to a local block list
Importable and shareable block lists (JSON or URL)
Per-site on/off toggle and a counter of items hidden

competitors.name: AI Content Shield
competitors.gap: Focused on blocking AI content and AI Overviews; not a general topic-mute tool with shareable crowdsourced lists across HN, YouTube and other sites.

competitors.name: Slopblock
competitors.gap: Firefox-only and experimental; YouTube-centred, so it does not cover topic muting on text-heavy sites like HN.

competitors.name: HN AI Source Filter
competitors.gap: HN-only, new, and with essentially no users or reviews yet.

ideas.title: LimitLens: AI plan usage and reset tracker for your phone
ideas.oneLiner: A Flutter app and home-screen widget that shows how much of your Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini plan limits you have left and when they reset.
ideas.problem: Paying users complain that AI plan usage limits are opaque and keep changing. Existing trackers are almost all free macOS menu-bar utilities, so nobody on Android or iOS can glance at remaining quota.
ideas.targetUsers: Paying Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini subscribers and indie developers who hit limits mid-work.
ideas.monetization: Free for one provider; Pro at about $2–3/month for multiple accounts, widgets and push alerts at custom thresholds.
mvp: Connect one or more provider accounts (official OAuth or API where available)
Dashboard of used and remaining quota with reset countdown
Push alert at 75% and 90% of the limit
Simple history chart of usage per week

competitors.name: AIQuotaBar
competitors.gap: macOS menu bar only and reads browser cookies, which is a privacy concern; nothing for phones.

competitors.name: Claude Usage Tracker
competitors.gap: Claude-only desktop app; no ChatGPT or Gemini and no mobile.

competitors.name: Mimir
competitors.gap: Freemium desktop tool covering several providers, but no mobile app or widget was found.
